decisions.reason: As a visible 2018 launch built on an already accepted machine concept, it carries prior investment and a positive installed-base signal, so management is very unlikely to withdraw it after only one year.

A stand-alone product-page launch suggests meaningful public commitment and development effort, and in this machinery business management would typically give such a new machine more time before admitting failure.
Although only mentioned rather than strongly promoted, it still fits the firm's core mobile processing portfolio and any weak early uptake can plausibly be treated as temporary in 2019.
The stationary electric fine shredder matches the firm's announced push toward tougher, resource-saving processing solutions, so strategic fit and sunk development costs favor continuation.

This is a narrower variant with less visible public commitment than the page-led launches, but it remains close to the firm's established green-waste and mobile machinery business, making an immediate withdrawal unlikely.

A dedicated web presentation and the capital-intensive nature of stationary pre-shredders imply substantial commitment, so management would be inclined to persist rather than write off the launch quickly.
